evidence_role: HCC-associated HBx mutation reported with genotype C2 risk signal
notes: HBx5 mutation was described as V5M/G1386A and discussed as a genotype C2 HCC risk factor.
C1653T is associated with increased HCC risk and maps to HBx H94Y.
T1753V can generate alternate HBx I127 substitutions; this row tests I127T.
T1753V can generate alternate HBx I127 substitutions; this row tests I127N.
T1753V can generate alternate HBx I127 substitutions; this row tests I127S.
A1762T/G1764A is one of the strongest HCC-associated HBV mutation signals and maps to HBx K130M/V131I.
HBx5+HBx130+HBx131 triple mutation was more common in HCC than CHB in a genotype C2 study.
JNCI 2009 reported A1762T/G1764A+C1653T combinations had high specificity for HCC prediction.
S166L was reported among HLA-DPB1*02:01 patients; PQ046054 genotype C1 large S has S at position 166.
G1896A was not associated with HCC in JNCI 2009, but associated in later BCP/precore meta-analysis; stop mutation needs a separate expression/truncation model.
PreS deletions are strongly associated with HCC but require indel-aware sequence analysis, not point-mutant peptide windows.
